column2: free building shapes kept; a part attached to a building must meet it through at least a 3x2 passage for belts, else the player is warned and it is not built; separate buildings at least one tile apart; networking adds +10% at first, +5% per Crimpatrice level

belts removed; a crew (2 at first, +1 per level) with one job each picked in the crew panel: machine operators run their machine, warehouse workers walk parts from the bar store and between machines to the crate on the routes they are given (one, some or all), IT staff wander at random between machines, the rack and a new PC station and keep the network bonus active; warnings when a needed job is empty; each machine is set to work raw bars or another machine's part

column2: more realistic cartoon look: light-shaded faces, soft shadows, concrete speckles and stains, brick tones, glass reflections, glowing stack lights, multi-tone grass, rounded shaded trees, corrugated sawtooth roofs, outlined pixel characters, screen vignette
cozy pixel-art look: the whole world drawn at low resolution and scaled up so its pixels match the characters', warm earthy palette with golden light, warm dark outlines, wooden interface panels

full art overhaul mixing a cozy farm look and a rustic one: plank floors, stone-and-timber walls with shelves, tools, notices and lanterns, lamp light pools, cream-and-iron riveted machines on wooden pallets, barn-like buildings with stone footing, boards, dark shingles and a braced door, dirt paths, bushes, stones, flowers and a fence, a day-night cycle with lit windows, plank UI with nails

intro flight over a little town, its industrial zone and into the small factory (skippable); back to one factory that grows in 4 bought stages by level, the meadow and drawn buildings removed from play
messier town in the intro: 1 to 3 houses per lot of mixed sizes, scattered off the grid, roofs both ways, some two-storey, parks, sheds, vegetable patches, picket fences, broken roads and dirt tracks

intro town redrawn as a European old town: a piazza with a fountain, a church with a bell tower and spire, a town hall with a clock tower and arcade, terraced pastel houses along winding cobbled streets (no grid), a river with a stone bridge, the industrial zone beyond

smooth town-to-industry edge (grass fades through worn earth to concrete, houses give way to workshops) and a varied, loosely laid industrial zone: brick factories with sawtooth roofs and smoking chimneys, sheds, silos, a water tower, container stacks, lorry yards, a railway with a goods train; clear ground round the player's factory

countryside round the town and the industrial zone, for a complete landscape: crop fields with furrows and hedges, farms with barns and haystacks, woods, hamlets along country roads that carry the streets on, the river running on both ways
column4: evidence/iteration-6-landscape.png (wide view taken with a test camera)

column2: story in five chapters: five ever bigger sites bought by level (wooden shed, brick workshop, works, modern factory, grand plant 16x12) with a flight from the old site to the new and a chapter card; machines move along; the town grows with the company (school, goods station, glass offices, supermarket, stadium, new houses, building sites with cranes); interior floor and walls change with the site

calendar of days and months with time at x1, x3, x8 (day-night follows it); each day machines age and may break, more often at speed: breakdowns repaired with the assembly minigame, machines past their age replaced for part of their price; the next site and the town's new buildings are built over the days and the site can be bought once the level is reached and the works are done

working day of 8 game hours (08:00-16:00 on the clock, factory closed at night); each shift hour every machine has a small chance to break; a warehouse zone of shelves in every site that grows with the chapter (2 to 12 shelves) and is empty after a move; raw bars come out of it, no longer free; an office desk opens the Ufficio panel with stock, orders (+10, +30, fill) delivered by truck after 2 hours and an automatic reorder; a stock chip under the clock

interior drawn crisp (pixel size 1 inside, sprites keep their pixel art); a door button "Esci in città (E)" opens the town around the factory with drag and zoom while time and production go on; floating signs over your factory (tap to go back in), the next site with its building percentage and days left, and the town building sites; worksites now rise day by day (slab, pillars, brick walls in scaffolding, roof) and the town buildings finish as the works progress

the 8-hour shift lasts 7 real minutes at x1; at 16:00 the clock stops (factory still, night light) until "Inizia il giorno dopo" (or N) starts the next day at 08:00; office and warehouse moved to a fixed wing beside the work floor, outside the cells where machines go: office desks at the back behind glass, shelves with aisles, a low yellow-black rail with a door, hanging signs; the wing grows with each site (6 to 24 shelves) and cannot be edited

no end-of-shift button: the night runs at the chosen speed with machines and crew stopped and no breakdowns; a stop/go button beside the speeds freezes time whenever the player wants (also F); HUD reorganised: clock, stop and speeds on top, crew and stock chips under them, level box top right, the goal is a small button under it that drops down the full text and pulses when a new goal arrives

bottom bar rebuilt: one strip with zoom and menu, work tools (Operatore, Demolisci), management (Squadra, Ufficio, Attrezzi, Ricette, each with its key and a red badge when something is missing), Città, the site switcher (name, chapter, free cells, arrows) and Negozio; the interface takes the look of the site you are in (wood, brick, riveted steel, blue glass, dark and gold) for HUD, bar and panels; buying a site creates a new empty factory with an empty warehouse while the old ones stay yours and keep producing; move between sites with the arrows or by tapping them in the town; warehouse workers and IT people can be sent to any site

office moved apart from the warehouse: the warehouse wing stays on the right, the office is a separate glass room in front of the factory with a gravel path to its door; when an order is due a lorry drives in beside the warehouse, a warehouse worker carries the bundles in while the load shrinks, the bars land on the shelves when it has unloaded, then it drives away; clerks sit at the office desks typing during the shift

office attached to the front of the factory again (its side wall continues the factory wall, glass with a door toward the floor), apart from the warehouse wing; clerks walk about the office and sit at a free PC for a while to type, only during the shift; the lorry arrives on a real road, unloads and leaves; around the plot there are now roads with kerbs and dashed lines, a crossing, a loading apron, other firms across the road (shed, containers, workshop, lorry park), an old brick works behind, houses and trees around
office gets a free aisle between the glass door and the desks, so no desk blocks the way in; the office is one row deeper at every site

unloading yard between the warehouse and the road (asphalt, bay lines, buffers, chevrons, SCARICO sign): the lorry comes along the road, reverses into the yard with its light blinking, unloads, drives out and away; town cars are drawn in depth order, steer round the fountain, drive on three streets in both directions and look like small cars; the railway runs from a buffer stop at the goods terminus to the edge of the map into a tunnel under a wooded hill, the train waits, runs east into the tunnel, stays hidden, then comes back out of the tunnel and returns

around the factory you now see the same part of town as on the map: the town is drawn under the interior, scaled so its site matches the factory (industrial ground, containers, river, silos, lorry park, railway, cars, train), without the invented houses and lawn; the factory stands on a concrete apron with the unloading yard and a short lane where the lorry comes and goes, fading in and out at the lane ends

entering a factory from the map is a zoom: the camera dives onto the site, then the inside opens from a little way out; leaving opens the map from close over the site; around the factory the close-up neighbourhood is invented but follows the map: each cell takes the map ground under it (industrial grey, dirt, grass), with water where the river is, streets where the map has them and the railway at the right place; free land is split into lots whose buildings follow the area (sheds, containers, workshops, silos, lorry parks where it is industrial; houses and trees toward town), worked out once per site

the lorry road to each warehouse is now part of the map: on the general map a paved road runs along the warehouse side of every site and joins the nearest street (nothing is built on it); close up the same road continues from the lane past the yard into the neighbourhood streets, and the lane is paved like the town streets so the two blend

skill web (Abilità, K): a token each level and two for each new site, spent one per node on a web of round nodes joined by braided cords around a centre; each machine has its branch (faster, precision for more valuable parts, high speed), plus warehouse and deliveries (cheaper bars, express lorry, bigger shelves, faster bar bench), crew (faster warehouse workers, carts, expert IT for more network bonus) and maintenance (fewer breakdowns twice, machines last longer); nodes open when the one before is yours and the level is reached; a side card shows what the node does and buys it; older saves get the tokens their level would have given

the skill web opens ring by ring: outer rings are under a dark fog with drifting clouds and a sign saying what opens them (level 3, second site, third site and level 5, fourth site and level 7); the next ring shows as question marks; the web is bigger and can be dragged; new outer nodes (taller shelving, own lorry fleet, forklift, dedicated server, diagnostics, full overhaul) and for each machine Mk II and Mk III nodes that unlock stronger versions in the shop (35% / 55% faster, higher quality, 2.5x / 5x the price) chosen with I / II / III buttons on the card; Mk machines carry a gold plate with their number

machines in five generations that look more professional and grow: Mk I 1x1 an old hand-cranked cast-iron machine on a wooden plinth with handwheels, belt drive, brass plate and oil can; Mk II 2x1 numerical-control years with green-grey paint, a long bed and a cabinet of round dials; Mk III 2x1 the first cream CNC enclosure with glass door and small screen; Mk IV 3x2 modern white panels, tool magazine drum, chip conveyor and a touchscreen on an arm; Mk V 4x4 a robot cell with the machine at the back, robot arm, pallet conveyor, safety fence and control station; machines now take every cell of their footprint (placement, moving, rotating, selling, walking round them, tapping, saving); the web has Mk II to Mk V nodes per machine (Mk V in a new ring opened by the fifth site and level 9); shop cards show the chosen generation, its size and price

a "Partita di prova: tutto sbloccato" button on the title screen starts a trial game with its own save: top level, all five sites with full warehouses and automatic reorder, every skill node, all tools at maximum, 5 million coins and 10 tokens; Continua and Nuova partita still use the real save

each kind of machine has its own shape and size in every generation: the saw is a long line with roller tables and later a bar magazine (up to 4x1, then 4x2 with a robot); the lathe is long with a headstock, then a bar feeder and a loading gantry (up to 4x2); the mill is square and tall with its head above the cabin, an umbrella tool magazine and a twin pallet changer (up to 3x3); the drill goes from a radial arm to a cabin with a tall column to a gantry with three spindles (up to 3x2); the 5-axis is the biggest, round window on the tilting table, chain tool magazine, robot cell (up to 4x4); fix: machine panel, minigames and skill nodes now show the real generation, and the sell price counts it

maximum level 50 (49 tokens from levels plus 8 from new sites = 57, the web has 51 nodes, so it can be completed); a steeper curve: XP for level L = 80 x (L-1)^2 (level 10 now needs 6480 XP instead of 1680, level 50 needs 192080); unlocks spread over the 50 levels: machines at 1, 3, 6, 9, 12, sites at 6, 14, 24, 34, network at 5, tool upgrades from 4 every 5 levels, web rings at 3, second site, third site + 15, fourth + 25, fifth + 35; one more person every two levels (26 at level 50) and the crew panel goes in pages of twelve; older saves keep their level

the crew is split by site: each site has a staff limit (6, 10, 14, 20, 28), the crew panel shows only the people of the site you are in, with a Sposta button to send someone to another site with room (their machine is left without an operator); new people go to the current site if there is room, otherwise to one with room, otherwise they wait and can be taken in where there is space; each site has a power supply (24, 50, 90, 150, 260 kW) and every machine draws power by kind (saw 4, lathe 6, mill 8, drill 5, 5-axis 12 kW for Mk I) and generation (x1.6, x2.2, x3.2, x4.5): a meter under the money shows it and the shop refuses a machine that would go over

fix: the tutorial no longer sends you to buy the Lathe before its level; until level 3 the guide says the Lathe opens at level 3 and to keep selling to gain experience, the goal shows the level progress, and the shop arrow appears only once it is unlocked

tapping the foreman (or his bubble) hides his advice and tapping him again shows it; while hidden a small bubble shows a dot, or a bouncing yellow exclamation mark when he has new advice; the choice is kept in the save; the shop arrows stay

offices like a modern open-plan office: white bench desks on steel legs with two monitors (charts, spreadsheets, drawings), keyboard, mug, desk plant or papers, acoustic screens with a coloured top, mesh chairs on five-star bases, carpet tiles, big potted plants, a water cooler, a printer, a whiteboard with sticky notes and a clock on the wall; at 16:00 every operator, warehouse worker, IT person and builder walks to the door and out to the street, at 08:00 they walk back in one after the other, and a machine starts only when its operator has reached it
